prompts.display_text: Pin This Is the Place, where Brigham Young entered the Salt Lake Valley in 1847.
prompts.text_original: Drop a pin on This Is the Place Heritage Park at the mouth of Emigration Canyon, where Brigham Young entered the Salt Lake Valley on July 24, 1847.

place.name: This Is the Place Heritage Park, Salt Lake City, Utah

prompts.citation: Church History Topics, Salt Lake Valley and Pioneer Trek, read 3 Nov 2026
prompts.summary: The vanguard pioneer company came down Emigration Canyon into the Salt Lake Valley in July 1847. Brigham Young, ill with mountain fever, arrived on July 24 and, by Wilford Woodruff's later account, said the valley was the right place. The This Is the Place Monument at the canyon mouth was dedicated in 1947 for the centennial.

prompts.display_text: Pin a monarchy with a dedicated temple. Commonwealth realms like Canada count.
prompts.text_original: A country with a reigning monarch as head of state (including Commonwealth realms) that has a dedicated temple (as of November 2026).
prompts.citation: ChurchofJesusChristTemples.org chronology and ChurchofJesusChrist.org temple list, read 3 Nov 2026
prompts.summary: Twelve monarchies have dedicated temples. Nine have their own royal house: Britain, Spain, Sweden, Denmark, the Netherlands, Japan, Thailand, Cambodia and Tonga. Canada, Australia and New Zealand count as Commonwealth realms with the British monarch as head of state. Belgium and Norway have temples under construction or announced but none dedicated.

answers.name: Australia
answers.fact: Commonwealth realm under the British Crown; five dedicated temples.

answers.name: Canada
answers.fact: Commonwealth realm under the British Crown; nine dedicated temples.

answers.name: United Kingdom
answers.fact: Kingdom; London (1958) and Preston (1998).

answers.name: Japan
answers.fact: Empire; four dedicated temples from Tokyo (1980).

answers.name: Spain
answers.fact: Kingdom; Madrid Spain (1999).

answers.name: New Zealand
answers.fact: Commonwealth realm under the British Crown; Hamilton (1958) and Auckland (2025).

answers.name: Tonga
answers.fact: Kingdom; Nuku'alofa Tonga (1983).

answers.name: Denmark
answers.fact: Kingdom; Copenhagen Denmark (2004).

answers.name: Netherlands
answers.fact: Kingdom; The Hague Netherlands (2002).

answers.name: Sweden
answers.fact: Kingdom; Stockholm Sweden (1985).

answers.name: Thailand
answers.fact: Kingdom; Bangkok Thailand (2023).

answers.name: Cambodia
answers.fact: Kingdom; Phnom Penh Cambodia (2026).

prompts.display_text: Pin a country where the Church or its members gave relief after a named hurricane, typhoon or cyclone, 1998 to 2019.
prompts.text_original: A country where members or the Church gave relief after a named hurricane, typhoon or cyclone (1998 to 2019).
prompts.citation: Global Histories (churchofjesuschrist.org), country chronologies and overviews, read 3 Nov 2026
prompts.note: Macau (Typhoon Hato 2017) omitted as a territory.
prompts.summary: Named storms set off member relief across the tropics: Hurricane Mitch in Honduras (1998), Iris in Belize (2001), Cyclone Pat in the Cook Islands (2010), Hurricane Irene in the Bahamas (2011), Typhoon Yolanda in the Philippines (2013), Cyclone Gita in Tonga (2018) and Cyclone Idai in Mozambique (2019).

answers.name: Philippines
answers.fact: 2013: members took part in extensive shelter and relief efforts during and after Typhoon Yolanda (Haiyan).

answers.name: Honduras
answers.fact: 1998: after Hurricane Mitch members directed a large-scale relief effort for members and nonmembers alike.

answers.name: Bahamas
answers.fact: 2011: Bahamian Saints assisted with relief efforts after Hurricane Irene.

answers.name: Mozambique
answers.fact: 2019: members helped reconstruct homes and clean streets after Cyclone Idai; the Maputo Stake donated essentials.

answers.name: Tonga
answers.fact: February 2018: after Tropical Cyclone Gita members and missionaries throughout Tonga helped clean up and rebuild.

answers.name: Belize
answers.fact: 2001: the Church sent relief supplies to areas of Belize still struggling after Hurricane Iris, which hit on October 8.

answers.name: Cook Islands
answers.fact: 2010: funds helped build new homes and water tanks after Cyclone Pat struck Rarotonga on February 9.

prompts.display_text: Pin a country where the Church's Perpetual Education Fund, loans for members' job training, began 2001-2005.
prompts.text_original: A country where the Church's Perpetual Education Fund (loans for members' vocational training) was introduced or first used between 2001 and 2005.
prompts.citation: Global Histories (churchofjesuschrist.org), country chronologies and overviews, read 3 Nov 2026
prompts.summary: President Gordon B. Hinckley announced the Perpetual Education Fund in 2001. Mexican and Chilean Saints were among its first participants; it reached the Philippines and Cape Verde in 2002, Bolivia in 2003 and DR Congo and Kenya in 2005.

answers.name: Chile
answers.fact: 2001: Chilean Saints helped pioneer the Perpetual Education Fund.

answers.name: Mexico
answers.fact: 2001: Mexican Saints helped pioneer the Perpetual Education Fund as some of the program's first participants.

answers.name: Philippines
answers.fact: February 2002: the Perpetual Education Fund was introduced in the Philippines.

answers.name: Bolivia
answers.fact: January 19, 2003: the Perpetual Education Fund was introduced in Bolivia.

answers.name: Kenya
answers.fact: 2005: young women and young men began using the Perpetual Education Fund to further their education.

answers.name: DR Congo
answers.fact: 2005: the Church's employment program, career workshops and Perpetual Education Fund were implemented.

answers.name: Cape Verde
answers.fact: 2002: members visited colleges to prepare for implementing the Perpetual Education Fund in Cape Verde.

prompts.display_text: Pin a country where the Bible records a named person being held in prison.
prompts.text_original: A present-day country where the Bible records a named person held in prison
prompts.note: Site is in the West Bank or Gaza; a player may reasonably pin ISR as well.
prompts.summary: Prisons mark the Bible's story from Joseph in Egypt to Paul in Rome. Jeremiah, Peter and Paul were all held in what is now Israel, Paul and Silas sang in the jail at Philippi (Acts 16:25), and two kings of Judah, Zedekiah and Jehoiachin, sat in Babylon's prison. Samson's captivity was at Gaza (Judges 16:21).

answers.name: Egypt
answers.fact: Joseph was put in Pharaoh's prison on Potiphar's accusation (Genesis 39:20).

answers.name: Israel
answers.fact: Jeremiah was jailed in Jerusalem, Peter in Herod's prison, and Paul two years at Caesarea (Jeremiah 37:15; Acts 12; 24:27).

answers.name: Greece
answers.fact: Paul and Silas sang in the Philippi jail before the earthquake (Acts 16:23-26).

answers.name: Italy
answers.fact: Paul lived in Rome under guard with a soldier (Acts 28:16).

answers.name: Iraq
answers.fact: Zedekiah died in prison in Babylon, and Jehoiachin was freed there after 37 years (Jeremiah 52:11; 2 Kings 25:27).

answers.name: Palestine
answers.fact: Samson ground grain in the prison house at Gaza, and Micaiah was jailed at Samaria (Judges 16:21; 1 Kings 22:26).
